transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-29 16:00 UTC / Duration 45m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Jane (CTO), Mark (ML), Omar (Infra), Sara (Product)
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda - sizing follow-up from last week's run, autoscale config, and next steps. Samir's gonna lead the sizing bits.
[00:18] Samir: cool, thanks. Mark you sent over the night-run csvs, I pulled out the p95 numbers - overall looks good, p95 around 220 to 260ms for the 8k context runs, token throughput roughly 120k tokens/min across the cluster. There was a couple of short spikes during bursts where latency jumped to ~700ms.
[00:41] Mark: yeah that was during the 2 minute burst we did at 02:14, we saw a queue build up. Not sure if that was cold start or autoscale latency.
[00:55] Samir: likely autoscale cooldown + provisioning. For Dedicated we recommend a min-reserved pool sized to cover steady-state QPS and a small burst buffer; then autoscale policies to add nodes when queue length crosses threshold.
[01:12] Omar: can you clarify "provisioning"? is that GPU spin-up or container scheduling time? We have strict SLOs so 700ms spikes are concerning.
[01:22] Samir: it's a combination. On our side provisioning a Dedicated machine includes scheduling, pulling quantized model artifacts and warming the KV cache; on infra there is also instance startup. We measure scale-in/out latency as ~45-90s to be safe in tests; so bursts shorter than that should be handled by pre-warmed capacity.
[01:45] Jane: So what's the recommended pre-warm ratio? We don't want to pay for a large idle cluster.
[01:51] Luis: a common pattern is set min_nodes to cover baseline 95th percentile plus a 20-30% burst buffer, and enable fast scale steps (e.g., 1-2 nodes) with short cooldowns for immediate scaling. Also enable prefix/KV caching to reduce token costs for repeated prompts.
[02:12] Mark: baseline 95th is about 3 GPUs today for our workload, with bursts up to 9 GPUs during midday. That delta is big. If min=3 and bursts go to 9, cost delta is non-trivial.
[02:27] Alex: that's where reserved capacity pricing helps — you commit to a baseline and get a lower per-hour rate, and bursts are billed as overage or on a burst capacity plan. We'll include a few scenarios in the sizing spreadsheet: conservative (min=3), moderate (min=5), and aggressive pre-warm (min=7) and show monthly costs.
[02:46] Sara: what's the burst billing model? Are bursts charged at on-demand rates?
[02:50] Alex: we have two options: burst pools (standby nodes billed at reduced rate but available immediately) or on-demand spin-up charged at on-demand price with a boot time. We can model both.
[03:03] Omar: for security, we need the network diagram and how peering works. Also KMS - we must use our HSM for keys.
[03:11] Samir: yes we support customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private mode; Dedicated can be configured to use your KMS via IAM roles and provide audit logs. I'll attach the network peering diagram and KMS notes.
[03:25] Jane: quick question on failure modes - if we hit capacity and autoscale can't keep up, what's the fallback?
[03:31] Samir: we have routing policies: canary to a smaller-but-latency-optimized model, or fallback to hosted model with higher cost but immediate capacity. We can also configure graceful degradation (reject large batch requests, queue with TTL).
[03:46] Mark: curious about queue TTL - what happens to requests that expire? We need clear behavior for SLA purposes.
[03:52] Samir: expired requests return a 429 with a short message; we can also surface metrics to trace which prompts were dropped. We'll include a recommended TTL and queue size in the spreadsheet.
[04:05] Alex: let's walk through the numbers briefly. We ran a test with average QPS 12, p95 240ms, token throughput 120k/min; to handle 2x burst for 10 minutes you'd need additional 6 GPUs equivalent. So min nodes at 3 + burst pool 6 would cover that.
[04:27] Mark: that matches our observed midday peaks but we normally don't sustain 2x bursts longer than 5 minutes. We could consider a buffer for short spikes and rely on autoscale for longer events.
[04:38] Priya: one operational note - for canary we recommend a 10-15% traffic split for 24-48 hours and run a smoke-check and quality eval on the responses. We'll help schedule that and provide an eval harness.
[04:53] Jane: timeline wise we want production in ~6 weeks. Is there anything blocking?
[04:58] Alex: primary blockers are finalizing sizing/pricing, customer benchmark for bursts, and VPC peering whitelists. Once we have those we can schedule Dedicated provisioning and a canary.
[05:12] Mark: I'll run an extended benchmark with a synthetic burst pattern to replicate the midday peak and push logs.
[05:18] Sara: also please include any recommended quantization profiles — we noticed perf gains when moving to int8 in earlier tests.
[05:25] Luis: noted, quantization tradeoffs will be in the spreadsheet - we'll show perf vs quality delta and recommended profiles per route.
[05:34] Jane: any concerns with multi-tenant data? We need assurance logs and audit trails.
[05:39] Samir: Dedicated gives instance-level isolation; logs can be exported to your SIEM and we provide token-level auditing. We'll include an example retention policy.
[05:49] Omar: what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[05:52] Alex: enterprise SLA available in contract; typically 99.9 uptime with latency objectives tied to config. For the POC we'll include an operational SLA doc.
[05:59] Mark: about benchmarks - do you want raw logs or processed metrics?
[06:03] Samir: raw logs help debug spikes, processed p50/p95 and traces are good for sizing. If you can push raw logs to the shared bucket that would be ideal.
[06:14] Alex: ok quick recap of action items - we'll send the sizing/pricing, Samir sends network/KMS docs, Mark runs extended benchmark, Priya schedules canary. Any other asks?
[06:27] Jane: please include estimated egress costs and any additional data transfer fees in the pricing.
[06:33] Alex: will do.
[06:35] Alex: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next week same time unless something else comes up.
[06:41] End meeting.
questions: What's recommended min_nodes vs burst pool sizing?
How long is autoscale provisioning and what's the cooldown?
What are fallback options when capacity is exhausted?
How will KMS/HSM integration work for Dedicated?
